info.name: MEXA Program Transfer — Gateway API
info.description:
The company's gateway (Node-RED PC, laptop, any program) and the MEXA server: **4 HTTPS calls, one token for all machines**.

| Call | |
|---|---|
| `GET /api/device/v1/status` | Every machine at once: machine_id, name, controller and its type (Fanuc / Mitsubishi), api_key, program path; program waiting? backup asked for? |
| `GET /api/device/v1/program?machine_id=ID` | Download the program waiting for that machine |
| `POST /api/device/v1/backup` | Upload a backup (multipart `machine_id`, `file`) |
| `POST /api/device/v1/report` | Program written / refused, backup could not be read |

**Set the variables** (collection → Variables): `baseUrl` = the server, e.g. `https://stmapi.stmcnc.com`; `token` = the company's gateway token (`mxg_…`, from S&T); `machineId` = a machine's `machine_id` as /status lists it.

How the gateway talks to the CNC (FTP, FOCAS, a folder, anything) is up to the gateway. Full guide: docs/PROGRAM_TRANSFER_API.md.

item.name: Gateway — the 4 calls (give this to the gateway team)
item.description:
Every call sends the company's token: `Authorization: Bearer {{token}}` (set on the collection). **One token for all machines**; S&T makes it. A call about one machine names it by its `machine_id`, as /status lists it.

**The gateway loop**

```
every 15 s:  GET /status                      ← one call, every machine
  for each machine with a program  → GET /program?machine_id=ID → write to the CNC (program_path)
                                   → POST /report {file_id, status: DONE}
                                     or {file_id, status: FAILED, message}
                                     next_program in the answer → the same again
  for each machine with backup_request → read the program from the CNC
                                   → POST /backup (machine_id, file)
                                     or POST /report {backup_request_id, status: FAILED, message}
```

Programs for one machine wait in line and go one after the other; different machines do not wait for each other.

Errors are always JSON: `{"status":"error","code":"…","message":"…"}`. 429 = too many calls: wait and try again.

item.name: 1. Status — every machine, poll every 15 s

request.description:
One call for **every machine** of the company — call it every `poll_seconds` (15 s).

- `machines[].program` is the program in front of that machine's line (`null`: nothing waiting). Download it (call 2), write it to the CNC, report it (3a / 3b).
- `programs_waiting` counts it and the ones behind it: two uploads for one machine go one after the other.
- `backup_request` is not null when someone pressed **Backup now**: read the program from the CNC and upload it (call 4a), or report that you could not (call 4b).
- `machine_id` names the machine in calls 2–4. `machine_ip` is its IP: the one its telemetry reports, else the **Machine IP** typed on the Machines page (`null` when neither is known).
- `controller_type` is the **Controller type** chosen on the Machines page: `FANUC` or `MITSUBISHI` (`null` when not chosen) — how to talk to that CNC.
- `controller_name` and `program_path` are the **Controller** and **Program path** on the Machines page (`null` when not filled in): the program path is the folder on the CNC, e.g. `//CNC_MEM/USER/PATH1/` on a Fanuc.
- `api_key` is the machine's telemetry key (MQTT topic `machines/{api_key}/telemetry`): keep this answer as private as the token.

The tests below pick the machine in the `machineId` variable (or the first one with something to do) and save `machineId`, `fileId`, `sha256` and `backupRequestId` for the next calls.

exec: const m = body.machines.find(x => x.machine_id === want) || body.machines.find(x => x.program || x.backup_request);
console.log('Nothing to do for any machine of ' + body.company + '.');

console.log(m.machine + ' (machine_id ' + m.machine_id + ', ' + (m.controller_type || 'controller type not set') + ', program path ' + (m.program_path || 'not set') + '): ' + m.program.program_name + ' waiting (' + m.programs_waiting + ' in line) → call 2. Download the program');
console.log(m.machine + ': backup asked for → read the program from the CNC and call 4a (or 4b on failure)');

request.description:
The program in front of the machine's line, as a file. Check `X-Sha256` against the file before writing it to the CNC. `X-File-Id` is the id to report.

After writing, report the result: **3a** (DONE) or **3b** (FAILED, with the reason). The report's answer names the machine's next program (`next_program`), which can follow at once.

exec: console.log(decodeURIComponent(pm.response.headers.get('X-Machine') || '') + ': ' + decodeURIComponent(pm.response.headers.get('X-Program-Name') || '') + ' — write it to the CNC, then report with 3a or 3b');

request.description:
The program is on the machine. The page shows **On the machine** and the person who uploaded it is notified. The program leaves the line; the answer's `next_program` is the machine's next one (`null`: nothing else waits).

`machine_id` is optional: sent, it must be the program's machine (`MACHINE_MISMATCH` otherwise). Sending the same report again (a retry after a lost answer) changes nothing: `"unchanged": true`.

exec: console.log(body.machine + ': next in line is ' + body.next_program.program_name + ' → call 2 again');

The program leaves the line all the same, so the next one is not held up; a corrected file is uploaded again.

request.description:
Multipart form data: `machine_id` and `file`. Answers that machine's open backup request (the person who asked is notified). A backup can also be sent without a request — after a change on the machine, or every night. A backup needs no report.

Text NC programs up to 20 MB; extensions `.nc .prg .cnc .txt .tap .eia .min .gcode .ptp .mpf .spf` or none (`O1234`).

item.name: 4b. Report — backup could not be read (FAILED)

request.description:
The backup could not be read from the CNC. The request is closed, the page shows **Backup failed** with the reason, **Backup now** works again and the person who asked is warned.

Only FAILED is reported here: a backup that worked is answered by uploading it (4a).

response.name: Recorded

item.name: Web side — to test the flow without the page (internal, do not share)
item.description:
Plays S&T's and the person's part, to run the whole flow from Postman: a → b (S&T makes the company's gateway token) → c → d → e (upload) → then the gateway calls 1, 2, 3a/3b → f (Backup now) → 1, 4a/4b.

Uses people's logins: remove this folder before sending the collection to the gateway team.

item.name: a. Sign in as S&T Super Admin

request.description: S&T's sign-in: only S&T makes a company's gateway token. Saves `sntToken`.

item.name: b. Make the company's gateway token (S&T)

request.description: Makes (or replaces) the company's one gateway token — what S&T Super Admin → Company Management → Gateway → Make token does — and saves it as `token` for the gateway folder. Shown once; the old one stops at once.
The token (its first characters only), when the gateway last called, from which address and with which agent.

exec: console.log(g ? (g.online ? 'Gateway online' : 'Gateway offline') + ', last call ' + g.last_seen_at : 'No token yet');

request.description: A person's sign-in (company admin), to play the web page's part. Saves `userToken`.

The company's machines, each with the program in front of its line (or the last one reported), how many wait, last backup and open backup request; beside them, whether the gateway is online. Saves the first machine as `machineId` unless set.

item.name: f. Upload a program (as the page does)

request.description: What **Upload program** on the page does: the file joins the end of the machine's line, and `/status` shows it when it is in front.

formdata.description: A program file, e.g. O1001.nc

item.name: g. Backup now (as the page does)

request.description: What **Backup now** on the page does: `/status` then shows a `backup_request` for that machine.

variable.description: The company's gateway token, from S&T (one for all machines)
A machine's machine_id as /status lists it (1. Status picks one with work when this one has none)
Set by a. Sign in as S&T
Web side folder only: the company's id (S&T → Company Management)
